clue.text: Range in European country (not Italy)

indicators.note: the bracketed not tells us to leave out the letter for Italy

parts.note: Spain is a European country
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A geography note: the range in question lies in a European country, not Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the full reach or extent of something, the same as its range.

clue.text: Appropriate observation on radio identifying political statements

indicators.note: broadcast on radio, words are only heard, so we want something that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: appropriate is proper, and an observation or look is a gander, giving proper gander

explanation.surface: A radio commentator spots and calls out the political spin in a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A gander, from 'take a gander', is informal British for a look. Said quickly, 'proper gander' matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is material put out to promote a political cause, often one-sided statements.

clue.text: Cut length keeping everything aligned

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the cut-plus-length pair holds the word for everything

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
all means everything

explanation.surface: Trimming a length of something while keeping all the pieces lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a verb acting on the length, but it supplies its own synonym; 'keeping' then holds 'everything' inside the cut-plus-length pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that are parallel run side by side the same distance apart, perfectly lined up.

clue.text: Rock guitarist to spoil rose?

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
rosé is a pink wine, and vin is French for wine, as in vin rosé

explanation.surface: Will a rock guitarist ruin a rose, perhaps by playing too loud?
explanation.walkthrough: Hank Marvin is the lead guitarist of the British band the Shadows. The question mark flags that 'rose' is the wine, vin rosé, not the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank Marvin is a famous rock guitarist, lead of the Shadows; here the name also nods to the theme robot.

clue.text: UK river between Nene and Dee, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the letters lying where the two river names meet are the end of Nene and the start of Dee, ne and de

explanation.surface: A river placed geographically between two other British rivers, the Nene and the Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reverses NEDE, the letters that straddle the gap from neNE to DEe, ignoring the linking and. The Nene and Dee are English and Welsh rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eden is a river in Cumbria, north-west England, so it is a British waterway.

clue.text: Vital oil bubbling? Limits to truly unpredictable behaviour

indicators.note: bubbling oil is churning about, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Hot oil that bubbles is truly unpredictable stuff in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbling' rearranges VITAL OIL into VOLATILI, and 'Limits to' gives T and Y, the first and last letters of truly.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatility is a tendency to change suddenly and erratically, which is behaviour hard to predict.

clue.text: Stick giving instruction regarding page layout

definitions.meaning: to stick to something is to cling to it
a page designer might write ... to show where an advertisement should be placed

explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast; split as ad here, it is a layout note telling where to place an advertisement.

clue.text: First-rate European capital backed introducing first of popular shops

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something into the middle of the reversed string
backed means turned round, so the first-rate term and the capital are read backwards

parts.note: A1, read as AI, means first-rate
Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of the word popular

explanation.surface: A guide to a top European capital and its popular shopping destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-rate' is A1, written with the letter I for the figure; 'backed' turns it round together with the capital, and 'introducing' brings in the first letter of popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is the plural of emporium, a large store or trading centre, so the word means stores.

clue.text: Operating system and staff involving one

indicators.note: involving means taking something inside, so the staff contains the word for one

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A computer user mentions their operating system and the staff who run it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' places the numeral for one within the staff; the surface's operating system is the real definition, a phone platform also used for a robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Android is Google's mobile phone platform, so it names a computer platform; it is also the theme robot's type.

clue.text: What bowler will do to score?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler runs in to the crease before delivering the ball
to ... a score or a bill is to accumulate it

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler's approach to the crease is his run-up; to run up points is to rack up a total.

clue.text: Saw about soldier following very good position?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the saw goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage

indicators.note: the soldier comes after, or follows, the letter for very

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant can stand for soldier

explanation.surface: Someone with a saw circling a soldier in a strong tactical spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool but a proverb, and a soldier ant is a warrior caste of ant. 'following' sets the insect after V, and 'about' wraps the saying round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a favourable position, such as being one point from winning a tennis game.

clue.text: Bat: good example of living creature

parts.note: in cricket, to bat is to be in, at the crease

explanation.surface: A bat is offered as a fine example of a living creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the flying mammal, but it is the cricket verb: a batsman is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is a single living thing, one instance of a creature.

clue.text: Always going to happen, even with reduced ability, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
reduced means cut short, so ability loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone whose powers are fading accepts that decline is bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims ability to ABILIT, and 'possibly' rearranges EVEN plus ABILIT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inevitable is certain to occur and cannot be avoided.

clue.text: Dildos, nothing less, strewn in road, a great heap

indicators.note: the scattered letters go inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a minor road

indicators.note: strewn means scattered about, so the letters are mixed up
less means without, so the zero is taken away

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of sex toys scattered across a road in a big pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops the zero from the toys, 'strewn' rearranges what remains into DSLID, and 'in' places that within the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is a mass of earth and rock that has slid down a slope, a huge mound of debris.

clue.text: One making video-call about various cars in part of city scene?

indicators.note: about means around, so the caller surrounds the mixed letters

parts.note: someone using Skype to make a video call could be called a Skyper

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of cars come in a different order

explanation.surface: A person on a video call chats about assorted cars seen in a city view.
explanation.walkthrough: Skype is a video-calling app, so its user is a Skyper. 'various' gives SCRA from the cars, and 'about' sets the caller round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscraper is a very tall building, a typical feature of a city skyline.

clue.text: Not an insider but not unknown for ever

indicators.note: not here tells us to drop the unknown from the word

parts.note: external means outside, belonging to someone not on the inside
X is the usual algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An outsider who is still known to everyone, it seems, for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Not' belongs to the phrase for an outsider; the second 'not' is the deletion signal removing X.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting without end, everlasting.

clue.text: Unusually pushy to exclude university backing for science in this field?

definitions.text: Unusually pushy to exclude university backing for science in this field?

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged
to exclude means to leave out, so the university letter is dropped
backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A pushy academic shunned by the university while backing a scientific discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude' takes U from PUSHY, 'Unusually' rearranges PSHY into PHYS, and 'backing for' turns SCI into ICS. The whole clue then describes a branch of science.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is a branch of science, the study of matter and energy, so it is a scientific field.

clue.text: Hurried round to one in flat, having deluded ideas

indicators.note: the three pieces go inside the flat

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or home
ran means hurried
O is round in shape
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone rushes over to a person in a flat who is gripped by delusions.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad is informal for a flat, a British apartment; 'in' places the hurried, round and one pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoid person suffers from irrational suspicion or delusions of persecution.

clue.text: Make space for time in holiday area?

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the holiday area

parts.note: the seaside is where many take a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone clearing their diary to fit a seaside holiday in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the seaside as just one example of a holiday area.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside room or money is to reserve it, keeping it free for a purpose.

clue.text: I knock fool around

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle is Phi, so I, the setter speaking, is Phi
a lander is a heavy blow or knock, as listed in Chambers

explanation.surface: A setter boasting of a knock while messing about.
explanation.walkthrough: In cryptics 'I' can stand for the setter, here Phi. LANDER as a blow is an unusual dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, playing about romantically.

clue.text: Depicts one engrossed nonsense, …

indicators.note: engrossed suggests absorbed inside, so the numeral sits within the nonsense

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone absorbed in nonsense describes it, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTS, besides underwear, is British slang for something worthless. The dots link to the next clue, which also uses nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to portray it, whether in pictures or in words.

clue.text: … nonsense left after jaunt

indicators.note: after means the left letter comes after the jaunt

parts.note: a drive is a jaunt or outing in a car

explanation.surface: Rubbish talk that remains after a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots carry on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly, meaningless talk, piffle.

clue.text: Point observed after display of sadness in burial chamber

indicators.note: the point is seen coming after the display of sadness

parts.note: to cry is to show sadness

explanation.surface: A mourner notices something after weeping in a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault beneath a church, used for interring the dead.

clue.text: I note mother avoiding cartoons etc, with feeling of exhaustion

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the mother is taken away

parts.note: animation covers cartoons and similar films
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Someone avoiding cartoons with their mother ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes the mother from the cartoon word, leaving ANITION; the definition describes weakness from lack of food, a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanition is exhaustion from lack of nourishment, a state of emptiness and weakness.

clue.text: What do you mean "Is a yob, primarily"?

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of yob is taken

explanation.surface: Someone indignantly asks whether they are being called a yob.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British word for a loutish youth. IS and A are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses surprise or protest, like asking someone to explain themselves.

clue.text: Article condemns unnamed US President

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unnamed means without the N that abbreviates name

parts.note: damns means condemns

explanation.surface: A news article condemns a US president who is left unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N, for name, from DAMNS.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both presidents of the USA.

clue.text: Name not used for single medicinal plant

indicators.note: not used means left out, so the name letter is dropped

parts.note: alone means single, on one's own

explanation.surface: A name is left out when a lone medicinal plant is labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not used' removes N from ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent whose sap is used in remedies for burns and skin.

clue.text: Growing bitterness recalled in match

indicators.note: the reversed bitterness sits inside the match

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for bitterness is read backwards

parts.note: gall is bitterness or resentment

explanation.surface: Resentment brought back into a sporting fixture keeps growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing' looks like an adjective but is the noun for cultivation; 'recalled' gives LLAG from the bitterness word, and 'in' sets it within the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land, preparing soil for crops; growing as a noun.

clue.text: One Church taking care of Lord without much warmth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A church takes on the care of a lord who proves rather unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the established church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-cold means extremely chilly, literally or in manner, with no warmth at all.
